questions.q: To generate an automatic Table of Contents, the document's headings must first be formatted with:
questions.solution: The TOC engine reads Heading 1-3 styles (and custom TOC styles). Manually bolded text carries no outline level, so it is ignored.
questions.shortcut: 'No style, no TOC' - the styles gallery, not formatting, feeds the TOC.

questions.q: VLOOKUP searches for the lookup value in which part of the table array?
questions.solution: VLOOKUP scans the first (leftmost) column of the table vertically and returns a value from the chosen column of the matching row. Searching along the first row is HLOOKUP.
questions.shortcut: V = Vertical = first column; H = Horizontal = first row.

questions.q: A file is selected in File Explorer. Pressing Alt+Enter will:
questions.solution: Alt+Enter opens the Properties dialog (size, location, dates, attributes). Enter opens the file, F2 renames it and Delete sends it to the Recycle Bin.

questions.q: The Wi-Fi wireless LAN standard family is designated by IEEE:
questions.solution: IEEE 802.11 covers Wi-Fi (a/b/g/n/ac/ax). 802.3 is wired Ethernet, 802.15 Bluetooth/PAN, 802.16 WiMAX.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: From French questionnaire: **double n** and the ending **-naire**. Questionaire loses an n; Questionnair drops the final e.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, "I bought a car yesterday."
options: He said that he had bought a car the previous day.
He said that he bought a car the previous day.
He said that he has bought a car yesterday.
He said that he had bought a car yesterday.
questions.solution: Simple past → **past perfect** (had bought); yesterday → **the previous day**. B stops at simple past; C keeps 'yesterday'; D shifts tense but strands 'yesterday' — both dimensions must move.
questions.shortcut: Past → past perfect, and yesterday travels to 'the previous day'.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (5).
questions.solution: The narrative continues in simple past sequence ('His colleagues laughed at first; later that day, half of them ___ him'): **joined**. It is the only finite past form; *joins* breaks the frame, *join* lacks agreement with 'half of them' in past narrative, and *joining* cannot act as the verb.
questions.shortcut: Narrative sequence: second event after 'laughed' takes plain past — no perfect needed in simple storytelling.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

She has been / working in this college / since ten years / and enjoys every day of it.
options: and enjoys every day of it.
questions.solution: *Since* takes a point of time (*since 2015*); a duration takes **for**: *for ten years*. The perfect continuous 'has been working' is itself correct with either partner — the partner is what failed.
questions.shortcut: Since = starting point, for = length. 'Since ten years' breaks the pair.

questions.q: India's only active volcano, Barren Island, is located in the:
options: Bay of Bengal off the Odisha coast
questions.solution: **Barren Island** lies in the **Andaman Sea**, east of the main Andaman islands. It is India's only confirmed active volcano; Narcondam nearby is dormant.

questions.q: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'?
questions.solution: **Norway** lies largely north of the Arctic Circle, where the Sun stays visible at midnight in summer. Finland is the 'Land of Thousand Lakes' and Japan the 'Land of the Rising Sun'.

questions.q: The Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet at which place to form the Ganga?
questions.solution: The Ganga is formed at **Devprayag** (Uttarakhand), the last of the Panch Prayag, where the **Bhagirathi** joins the **Alaknanda**. Rudraprayag is the Alaknanda–Mandakini confluence; Karnaprayag is the Alaknanda–Pindar confluence.
questions.shortcut: 'Very Nice Kids Read Daily' — D = Devprayag, the final meeting.

questions.q: Which of the following rivers flows westward through a rift valley and drains into the Arabian Sea?
questions.solution: The **Narmada** rises at **Amarkantak** and flows **west** between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in a **rift valley**, entering the **Gulf of Khambhat** (Arabian Sea) through an estuary. The other three flow east into the Bay of Bengal and form deltas.

questions.q: A man spends 80% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure increases by 10%. The percentage increase in his savings is:
questions.solution:
Take income = 100 ⇒ expenditure = 80, savings = 20.
New income = 115, new expenditure = 88 ⇒ new savings = 27.
Increase $= \frac{7}{20} \times 100 = 35\%$.
questions.shortcut: Track the three quantities on income = 100. Savings go 20 → 27 = +35%.

questions.q: The surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm is: [Use $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution: $S=4\pi r^2=4\times\frac{22}{7}\times49=616$ sq cm.
questions.shortcut: $4\times154=616$. Trap: 462 is the hemisphere TSA ($3\pi r^2$); 308 is $2\pi r^2$.

questions.q: A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. The quantity of water in the mixture is:
questions.solution: Water $= 40 \times \frac{1}{4} = 10$ litres.

questions.q: Find the missing term: **3, 8, 15, ?, 35, 48**
questions.solution: Differences: 5, 7, 9 then 13 — the middle gap must be **11** (odd numbers). So ? = 15 + 11 = **24**. (Terms are n² − 1: 2²−1 = 3, ..., 7²−1 = 48.)
questions.shortcut: Ladder both ways: the difference row 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 must stay symmetric around the gap.

questions.solution: The correct figure sits in the **upper-centre part** of the given figure, with every line matching in direction and length. The other three options are the same shape shown as its mirror (left-right flip), a water image (top-bottom flip) and a copy turned through 90 degrees — none of them can be traced in the figure without turning it, and rotation is not allowed.
questions.shortcut: Fix the most distinctive stroke (a lone diagonal or an odd-length line), locate it in the main figure, then check the rest.

questions.q: Find the next letter: **A, C, B, D, C, E, ?**
questions.solution: Steps alternate: +2, −1, +2, −1, +2 → next −1. E(5) − 1 = **D**.
questions.shortcut: A saw-tooth step row (+2, −1 repeating) — extend the cycle, don't average.
questions.pattern: letter series — constant or rising step

questions.q: **Rani walks 7 km North, turns right and walks 7 km East, then turns right and walks 7 km South.** What is her position relative to the start?
questions.solution: North 7 and South 7 cancel; the East 7 km survives → she is **7 km East** of the start. (21 km is the distance walked.)
questions.shortcut: Out-and-back legs cancel; only the middle leg counts.
questions.pattern: direction of the endpoint from start
